# Packetlyzer

FFXI Packet Capture and Analysis Tool — real-time packet decoder with NPC/item/zone lookup, byte tracking, and reverse engineering workbench.

## Thanks: 
BalladOfWorms - OmniWatch, POLUtilis Contributors, ZeromusXYZ - VieweD, atom0s - many many things. And the entire FFXI LSB community. 

## Background: 

I created this tool in hopes of making it easier for people contributing to LSB Development. This was created with AI (AWS Kiro) and using Repos of other addons and utility tools. 

I work in the Automotive world with experience on Automotive Software, Diagnostics and CAN/LIN/Automotive ETH Communication so I figured I would try to bring that experience into making a tool to help understand C>S and S>C Packets. 

This is my first publically released program, so I appreciate any and all feedback. There is many many more things to be added and updated but I feel like its at a point to release it to start getting feedback on what things to improve and features to add. 

Similar to capture packet log files and viewing them in VieweD, this is aimed to seeing packets in Real-Time on a 2nd or split screen. There is the option to record the log file and load it in VieweD. 

You can add Opcodes to be filtered if you want to focus on certain packets, scroll through the history of a packet to see how the data is changing. The Reverse Engineer tab is still underwork, the intent with that is to view the pinned byte/bit data and create/modify database in real time. 

There is some built in DAT File referencing. For example when you see a campaign status update, the server references to DAT File to display the text, so the Resolved Text tab should show the same data, so will need to point to your FFXI Installation if it's not in the default Windows install location. The NPC ID Lookup will likely not work as it is using the SQL database built from LSB. One goal is to commonize the database into one file type, be it SQL, XML, or something standarized like .DBC.

The packet stuff is new to me, I am approaching this how I would if I am reverse engineering CAN Signals on a benchmark vehicle. So for me to understand what is going on, I need to see in real time what data is changing when performing or seeing an action happening. Again, I am open to any and all suggestions for changes and additions. 

## Features

- **Real-time packet capture** via Windower 4 or Ashita v3/v4 addon
- **Decoded field display** with position, type, value, raw hex, and DB lookup
- **NPC/Mob ID resolution** from server SQL (40K+ entities)
- **Auto-lookup** for items, zones, models, jobs, spells, weather
- **Chronological and Fixed Position** display modes
- **Packet history navigation** with slider for browsing opcode history
- **Byte Tracker** for monitoring changing data across packets
- **Reverse Engineer workbench** for defining custom signal interpretations
- **Hex dump** with persistent positional highlighting
- **Export, filtering, and logging** capabilities

## Download

Download the latest release from the [Releases](https://github.com/Exolis/Packetlyzer/releases) page.

Extract `Packetlyzer-win64.zip` and run `Packetlyzer.exe` — no Python install required.

## Addon Setup

Copy the `addon/` folder contents to your Windower or Ashita addons directory:

**Windower 4:**
```
windower/addons/packetlyzer/
├── packetlyzer.lua
├── compat.lua
└── serialize.lua

Load in-game: //lua load packetlyzer
```

**Ashita v3/v4:**
```
Ashita/addons/packetlyzer/
├── packetlyzer.lua
├── compat.lua
└── serialize.lua
```

Load in-game: `/addon load packetlyzer`

Run the executible for the UI. It's quicker to run the .exe first then load in FFXI. It may take a minute to connect if you load addon before running the exe. 

## Running from Source

```bash
# Requires Python 3.12+
pip install PyQt6
python packetlyzer.py
```

## Building the Executable

```bash
pip install pyinstaller
pyinstaller packetlyzer.spec --noconfirm
# Output: dist/Packetlyzer/Packetlyzer.exe
```

## NPC Lookup (Optional)

For entity ID resolution, point the tool at your server's `sql/` directory containing `npc_list.sql`. The tool auto-searches common paths.
